item.title: Compare two shipping trial measures
item.summary: A warehouse planner and analyst discuss a faster dispatch trial with an unexpected side effect.
item.transcript_text:
Planner: The first scan is happening twenty minutes earlier, so on paper the new schedule works.
Analyst: That's the moment the box leaves packing, not the moment it moves onto a van. Units now reach the loading bay before the vans do. By the end of the shift, more boxes are being switched between routes at the bay.
Planner: Are you saying we should go back to the old timetable?
Analyst: Keep the early shift on Tuesday, when van arrival is predictable, and use the old schedule on other days as a comparison. Log the actual departures and re-routing, not just the first scan.
Planner: Good. If the benefit survives that test, we can talk about adding days.

questions.prompt: What problem does the analyst identify?
options: The early shift is costing twice as much
The improvement measures only an early stage
The vans now leave earlier than packing
The scan equipment is broken
questions.explanation: The scan precedes loading and can miss a bottleneck at the bay.

questions.prompt: What happens more often on the new schedule?
options: Boxes change routes at the loading bay
Vans reach the warehouse late on Tuesday
Boxes return to the packing room
Workers skip all scans
questions.explanation: The analyst notes an increase in switching boxes between routes.

questions.prompt: Why keep the early shift on Tuesday?
options: Tuesday is the only day with working scanners
Boxes need no labels then
A new van arrives every Tuesday
Van arrivals are predictable that day
questions.explanation: Predictable van arrivals make it a useful condition for the trial.

questions.prompt: What data would make the second trial more informative?
options: Truck fuel prices and packing wages
Only the first scan for each route
Actual departures and re-routing as well as scan times
The number of van drivers at lunch
questions.explanation: The proposed metrics cover later steps and complications.

questions.prompt: What would justify expanding the trial?
options: Completing Tuesday without rerouting any box
A benefit that persists after fuller measurement
The first scan staying exactly twenty minutes early
A permanently identical arrival time on every day
questions.explanation: The planner says expansion depends on the measured improvement surviving.

children.segment_text: on paper the new schedule works
units now reach the loading bay
we can talk about adding days
